Our multi-model council costs way more than expected and is slow — how do we cut cost without losing quality?
expected_behavior: leads with route-first gating: a cheap classifier/router in front so the expensive council path only fires on the hard tail, not every query
recommends calibrating the escalation threshold on the team's own traffic (ECE/Brier vs ground truth) rather than trusting a default cutoff
suggests structuring council prompts with a shared static prefix so all member calls hit prompt caching
frames the goal as cost-per-resolved-outcome and tells the user to re-measure any cited multiplier or percentage on their own workload rather than trusting it blindly
does not recommend routing on a member's raw self-reported confidence

cases.prompt: We want to route easy queries to a cheap model and only escalate hard ones to the full council — how should we design that?
expected_behavior: proposes a routing ladder: semantic/embedding router for known intents, then a learned router, escalating below a confidence/similarity threshold
warns that routing on raw self-reported confidence is unreliable and can be inversely correlated with correctness on hard tasks — calibrate the threshold instead
flags that learned routers degrade on out-of-distribution traffic and need retraining whenever the model pool changes
mentions peer disagreement among cheap members as a stronger escalation signal than any single member's self-reported confidence

cases.prompt: Our agent's tool-use loop burns a lot of tokens per turn — should we re-route to a cheaper model every turn to save money?
expected_behavior: advises against re-routing mid-session inside an active tool-call loop because it breaks prompt-cache locality and can invalidate in-flight tool-call sequences
recommends locking the model for the duration of the active loop and re-routing only at session or task boundaries
distinguishes this from council fan-out cost and notes agent/multi-agent token multipliers are a separate, larger overhead than a single extra council call

cases.prompt: One slow model in our council is dragging down our overall response time even though the others finish fast — how do we fix tail latency?
expected_behavior: explains that fan-out wall-clock time is bounded by the slowest member, so the tail-latency member dominates the council's overall latency
recommends budgeting P95/P99 latency rather than averages
suggests TTFT-based hedging triggers instead of static timeouts, with hedge load capped (e.g. around a 10% token-bucket)
clarifies that parallel dispatch only helps latency, not cost — the tokens for every member are still paid for regardless of wall-clock time
